name: Dmitry Rybolovlev

summary.text: Dmitry Rybolovlev is a Russian businessman. In 2008 he bought the Palm Beach oceanfront estate known as Maison de l'Amitié from Donald Trump for a recorded $95 million; Trump had bought it from the bankruptcy estate of Abe Gosman in November 2004 for about $41 million. Rybolovlev's spokesman has said the property was acquired for investment purposes by a family trust. The house was demolished in 2016 and the land sold as three lots between 2016 and 2019. In February 2018 Senator Ron Wyden asked the Treasury Department for records relating to the transaction; Rybolovlev's spokesman said there was no suggestion of impropriety.

facts.claim: In November 2004 Donald Trump bought the Palm Beach estate Maison de l'Amitié from the Chapter 7 bankruptcy estate of nursing-home operator Abe Gosman for about $41 million ($41.35 million per PBS), outbidding Jeffrey Epstein at the auction.
facts.quote: Trump snapped up the property from Gosman's Chapter 7 Bankruptcy Estate for $41 million.

sources.title: That time a Russian billionaire paid Trump $95 million for a mansion

facts.claim: In 2008 Trump sold the Maison de l'Amitié estate to Dmitry Rybolovlev for a price documented in Palm Beach County courthouse records as $95 million, after renovations the Palm Beach Post described as mostly cosmetic.
facts.quote: Trump carried out renovations — mostly cosmetic — to the mansion before selling the estate in 2008 for what was then documented in courthouse records as $95 million to Russian billionaire Dmitry Rybolovlev.

facts.claim: Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc. filed a voluntary Chapter 11 petition in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of New York on September 15, 2008, about two months after the 2008 Palm Beach sale.
facts.quote: Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on September 15, 2008, according to its own SEC filings.

facts.claim: A spokesman for Rybolovlev, Brian Cattell, said the Palm Beach property was bought as an investment by the Rybolovlev family trust.
facts.quote: "The property was acquired for investment purposes by the Rybolovlev family trust, as was clearly stated at the time of the purchase in 2008," according to Brian Cattell, a New York-based spokesman for Rybolovlev.

sources.title: Trump in Palm Beach: Why did Russian pay so much for his mansion?

facts.claim: On February 9, 2018 Senator Ron Wyden, ranking member of the Senate Finance Committee, wrote to the Treasury Department requesting financial records relating to Rybolovlev's purchase of the Trump Palm Beach property, noting that the 2008 sale price was more than double what Trump had paid four years earlier.
facts.quote: the 2008 sale more than doubled the price Mr. Trump paid for it just four years earlier

facts.claim: Senator Cory Booker wrote to Treasury Secretary Mnuchin describing the 2008 sale as $30 million above known appraisals and paid in an all-cash transaction through a shell company, and asked for more information on the transaction.
facts.quote: the sale was $30 million above known appraisals and was paid in an all-cash transaction through a shell company

sources.title: Booker urges Mnuchin to provide more information on Trump administration's ties to Russian oligarch

facts.claim: Responding to the 2018 Senate inquiries, Rybolovlev's spokesman Brian Cattell said the transaction had been publicly announced and widely covered and that there was no suggestion of any impropriety about the purchase.
facts.quote: "The transaction was publicly announced and widely covered by the U.S. media," said Brian Cattell, spokesman for the oligarch. "There was no suggestion whatsoever of any impropriety about the purchase."

sources.title: Trump property sale with Russian probed

facts.claim: Rybolovlev and Trump have both denied knowing each other and have said their only transaction was the sale of the Palm Beach mansion.
facts.quote: Rybolovlev and Trump have denied knowing each other and said their only transaction involved the sale of his Palm Beach mansion.

sources.title: Russian who bought Trump mansion mired in big scandal

facts.claim: Rybolovlev never lived in the house; he had it razed and the 6.26-acre site divided into three lots, which sold for about $108.2 million combined, the last in July 2019.
facts.quote: Rybolovlev bought the 6.26-acre estate from Trump in 2008 for $95 million, then razed a mansion on the property and divided the land into three separate lots.

sources.title: Rybolovlev sells last piece of Trump's ex-Palm Beach estate

facts.claim: The northernmost of the three lots sold for $34.34 million in 2016, and a two-acre lot at 535 North County Road sold for $37 million in October 2017 to a Boca Raton company linked to builder Mark Pulte.
facts.quote: The two-acre lot at 535 North County Road had been listed for sale for $39.8 million. The new owner of the lot is a Boca Raton company linked to Mark Pulte of luxury home building firm Mark Timothy Inc.

openQuestions: The buying entity is widely given as County Road Property LLC and the closing date as July 16, 2008, but no source reached in this session (other than reference sites) stated these; check the Palm Beach County Clerk official records for 515 North County Road.
Trump was reportedly quoted in 2008 saying 'I love breaking records, and this is a record'; the original Palm Beach Post/Daily News article was not reached.
Rybolovlev's 2011 divorce-case deposition reportedly stated the house was owned by a family trust for his daughters; the court record was not reached.
The demolition date (March 2016 per one listing site; architectural commission approval April 2016) should be checked against Town of Palm Beach records.
Trump Organization: no source in this session named the Trump Organization as a party to the 2008 sale, so no connection was recorded.
